basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 6.' and it opens '(Vers. 6.) In nomine fratrum suorum vocabuntur in haereditatem suam. Non, inquit,'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 6.) In nomine fratrum suorum vocabuntur in haereditatem suam. Non, inquit, accipient separatim terram, nec funiculos proprios habebunt, ut reliquae tribus, sed in tribubus Ephraim et Manasse, quasi appendices populi commiscebuntur.
